title: One understanding per unit, linked by ideas
statement: Give each unit one explicit primary understanding with its likely misconceptions, and link units by the ideas they share rather than by shared words or names.
detail: The course-plan quality standard asks whether a sequence builds and reuses knowledge deliberately; it accepts one that names its primary understanding, what each part adds and a later activity that needs that knowledge, and lists links based only on shared words among its failure signals (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, Q014). Its obligations include giving every unit one primary understanding and using conceptual rather than surface cross-unit links. The Grade 3 reading criteria require cross-unit links stated as the big idea, not as surface facts such as matching names (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D10-delivery-ux-accessibility.md`). Done this way, the build-up of knowledge across units can be seen.
